subject: Observability routing & evidence transfer for ACME private deployment
messages:
From: Jenna Park <jenna.park@acme.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@acme-corp.com
Date: 2029-10-02 09:12 -0700
Subject: Observability export requirements for private VPC deployment

Alex — thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. A few follow-ups from our security and SRE teams about logs/traces leaving our VPC to Redwood's observability pipelines: 

- Our constraints: no persistent egress to public endpoints; we need a signed, pull-based transfer (SFTP or signed bundle fetch) for archived evidence; live telemetry should be forwarded to our self-hosted Splunk HEC endpoint inside the VPC.
- Retention and chain-of-custody: we must retain raw request/response logs + traces for 90 days in immutable storage and provide a verifiable transfer log to auditors.
- Encryption: in-transit TLS1.3 mandatory; at-rest encryption per our KMS policy.
- Tracing hooks: we want Redwood to emit OTLP-compatible spans with required fields: request_id, model_version, node_id, and sampling flags.

Can you confirm what changes are required on the private agent and what the onboarding timeline looks like? I attached the high-level compliance checklist.

—Jenna

Attachments: acme-obsv-requirements-2029-10.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Jenna Park <jenna.park@acme.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-10-02 10:03 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability export requirements for private VPC deployment

Jenna — quick response to confirm receipt and summarize our plan: 

1) Live telemetry: Redwood Private agent (sidecar) supports pushing directly to customer-run HEC endpoints. We'll add a connector shim that (a) authenticates using a client cert you provide, (b) enforces TLS1.3, and (c) includes per-event signed headers for integrity.

2) Traces: we'll enable OTLP gRPC export by default in the private package and extend the span schema to include request_id, model_version, node_id. Sampling will be configured at the agent; we can provide both head-based and tail-based configs.

3) Evidence transfer: for audited bundles (raw logs + KV caches) we'll stage immutable tarballs inside the customer's S3-compatible endpoint or expose a signed, short-lived presigned URL that your auditor can pull. We'll also emit a signed transfer manifest (SHA256 + signature) to meet chain-of-custody.

4) Retention: Redwood will not retain copies of raw logs unless explicitly requested; by default we only forward. If you need Redwood to store evidence under contract (e.g., for forensic support) we will follow the KMS keys you supply and limit retention.

I'll loop in Lauren to confirm the exact cert handling and Ben for Splunk config specifics. Proposed onboarding milestone: connector PR + test harness by Oct 11, signed cert exchange by Oct 15, HEC verification in staging Oct 18–20.

—Alex

Attachment: redwood-evidence-guide.pdf (application/pdf)

From: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: alex@redwood.com, ben@redwood.com, marcus@redwood.com
Date: 2029-10-02 11:20 -07:00
Subject: RE: Observability export requirements for private VPC deployment

Alex/Ben/Marcus — notes from brief sync with security: 

- Client cert handling: we must validate SAN entries and tie cert thumbprints to the HubSpot deal record (ACME-3241). No wildcard certs.
- Network: the sidecar will open only outbound on 443 to the internal HEC FQDN; we'll provide a hardened outbound allowlist rule set that your network team can apply to the NAT gateway.
- Splunk HEC: Ben, please create a minimal HEC ingestion example that includes expected headers and sample events (include both JSON metadata + raw token payload). Jenna — can you point us to the internal HEC FQDN and whether HTTP auth or cert mutual TLS is required?

Marcus — flagging retention/immutable store design. We should provide a non-opinionated playbook for customers who want to keep evidence outside Redwood but still need transfer manifests. Draft attached.

—Lauren

Attachment: vpc-evidence-transfer-playbook.md (text/markdown)

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Jenna Park <jenna.park@acme.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-10-04 17:03 -07:00
Subject: Final plan: HEC connector + evidence transfer flow (next steps)

Jenna — thanks for the clarifications over the last 48 hours. Below is our agreed plan and action items so you can share with your auditors and SRE: 

Summary of deliverables:
- Splunk HEC connector (mutual TLS + client cert auth) — config sample attached (splunk-hec-connector-config.yaml).
- OTLP span schema update — we will ship a patch that adds request_id, model_version, node_id and ensures 1:1 mapping to your trace IDs.
- Evidence transfer: signed, immutable tarball flow with presigned URL + manifest (SHA256 + Redwood signature). Optionally we can stage into your S3 compatible bucket if you provide write credentials and a bucket ARN.
- Audit artifacts: transfer manifests, connector verification logs, and a signed operator acceptance file.

Action items / Owners / Dates:
- Jenna: share HEC FQDN and whether cert mTLS is required (by 2029-10-07).
- Ben (Redwood): produce HEC ingestion example & test harness (by 2029-10-11).
- Alex (Redwood): PR for connector shim + OTLP schema change (by 2029-10-11).
- Lauren (Redwood): produce cert validation checklist and HubSpot record update (ACME-3241) (by 2029-10-09).

Security notes (important for auditors):
- All exports will only use TLS1.3 or equivalent; mutual TLS supported for HEC.
- We will sign transfer manifests with Redwood's rotating KMS key; if you require we can sign with your KMS via delegated signing workflow.
- We will include a per-transfer certificate chain and timestamped signature to support your immutability requirements.

I'll attach the Splunk sample and the evidence guide; we can run a joint verification session next week.

Thanks — Alex

Attachments: splunk-hec-connector-config.yaml (text/yaml), redwood-evidence-guide.pdf (application/pdf)
